How much does garage door replacement cost?

Swapping the old door for a new one — what it costs, and what moves the price:

$754–$1,707

National average $1,231

Bay Area: $1,030–$2,017 (avg $1,502) — about 22% above national; skip wood here, the fog eats it.

Why quotes run $750 to $8,000

Material
Steel is the default and the cheapest. Wood runs $1,200–$4,000+ for a standard 16×7 door — and needs maintenance the fog will punish.
Size
Single-car doors are the baseline. Double doors need more material, heavier hardware, and stronger springs — and cost meaningfully more.
Insulation
Insulated doors cost $200–$600 more than non-insulated. Worth it for attached garages; skip it for a detached one.
Opener & extras
A new opener adds $350–$1,000 in San Francisco; smart openers run up to $1,300 for the unit alone. Windows and decorative hardware stack on top.

Steel or wood

Steel
$754–$1,700

The workhorse: affordable, low-maintenance, takes insulation well. What most homes get.

Wood
$1,200–$4,000+

Beautiful, heavy, and maintenance-hungry — San Francisco's fog punishes it. Worth it for historic homes; overkill otherwise.

Bottom line: insulated steel is the rational pick for most homes. Wood only if the house demands it — and budget for the upkeep.

Common questions

How long does garage door replacement take?

A few hours for a standard swap. Custom sizes, structural fixes, or opener wiring can stretch it to a full day.

Can I replace a garage door myself?

Don't. The springs hold enough tension to seriously injure you, and misaligned tracks wreck the opener. This is pro work.

Should I get an insulated door?

Yes for an attached garage — it steadies temperatures and quiets the street. For a detached garage you barely use, save the $200–$600.

How long does a garage door last?

About 10–20 years with maintenance. Springs wear first; lubricate the moving parts yearly and the door lasts longer.

Every garage prices differently.
